paragraphs.text: Opinions differ on whether cyclists should be required by law to wear helmets. Dr Anna Berg, a surgeon, argues that helmets prevent many serious head injuries and that a law is the only way to make people wear them. Transport researcher Tom Hale agrees that helmets protect individuals, but he points out that when one city made them compulsory, the number of people cycling fell by a third. Mia Chen, who runs a cycling charity, believes that safer roads would do more for cyclists than any helmet law.
